openings.claim: Fixed numbered storage addresses could transfer location recall and surname-region search from the clerk to a behind-desk paper address system, while the existing clerk retains identity verification and every handoff.
openings.delta: Number bounded locations on the existing shelves and cart using paper divider cards. A behind-desk sheet links the entitled reader to the numbered location; an assigned hold stays there until pickup. The physical address carries location stability, so retrieval follows one pointer instead of interpreting household surnames or reconstructing moves. Maintenance requires recording each arrival and clearing its address after collection; the clerk must check the reader association and manage capacity. This evaluates an unproven intervention, not an observed improvement.
openings.prediction: Where assigned addresses remain usable, second-location searches decline even for household-name mismatches; cart holds need not migrate to shelves to become retrievable.
openings.rival_prediction: The nearest alternative is retaining surname storage and updating the exception slip after every move. If stale records alone explain delays, that alternative should improve retrieval equally; fixed addresses would add no advantage after records are kept current.
openings.defeat: A bounded comparison finds persistent second-location searches despite accurate fixed addresses, or stable addressing requires more than ten daily preparation minutes, unavailable storage capacity, or a wrong-reader handoff.
openings.probe: Use paper, pencils and the existing timing sheet for a bounded trial covering the stipulated evening concentration. Stop preparation at ten clerk-minutes; if setup is incomplete, record a failed feasibility probe. Keep all identity information behind the desk, use only existing storage, and retain clerk handoffs. Record address errors, movements forced by capacity, preparation time, corrections and pickup duration. Compare with a period using promptly updated exception records; do not infer the 95% target from the supplied synthetic samples.
assumptions: Usable numbered locations can accommodate actual book sizes and arrival volume without adding furniture.
Accurate reader-to-hold associations are available or can be established by the clerk.
Address creation and maintenance fit the ten-minute daily preparation limit; the eight-minute sample does not establish this.
